court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Nagpur, Case No. unknown
case_name: Dharmendra S/O Bansilal Jain v. Mrs. Nidhi Dharmendra Jain (Choudhary)

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Dharmendra Bansilal Jain (husband), Business, R/o 44 Prasadnagar, Bhamti, Nagpur - 440 016
parties.respondent_defendant: Mrs. Nidhi Dharmendra Jain (wife), Business, R/o 49, Bajajnagar, Shri Narayan Complex, Nagpur

facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1991 and had two children. The husband moved out of the matrimonial house in 2012. The wife filed an application seeking direction to pay college and school fees of their sons.

legal_principles.principle: Maintenance can be granted to major sons under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: Considering the aspect of Section 26 of the Hindu Marriage Act, the learned Judge, Family Court then by observing that there was no impediment for the Court to grant maintenance under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act to major sons, rejected the application.
cited_cases: B. (Husband) v. A. (Wife), (Year) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: The court can grant interim maintenance to children pursuing education.
legal_principles.held: The learned Judge directed the petitioner/husband to pay an amount of Rs.5,000/- per month to each son i.e. total Rs.10,000/- per month towards interim maintenance from the date of application i.e. 14.07.2014.
use_in: divorce cases involving children's education expenses

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order allowing the wife's application under Section 24 read with Section 26 of the Hindu Marriage Act was upheld.

use_for_drafting: seeking waiver of notice in divorce case
